sentences.text: Corythosaurus was estimated to be between 7.7 and 9 meters long, with a skull and crest reaching a height of 70.8 centimeters.
One preserved specimen contained the remains of its last meal, including conifer needles, seeds, twigs, and fruits, found inside its chest cavity.
Scientists speculate that this dinosaur could produce loud, low-pitched calls resembling a trombone or wind instrument by exhaling through its nasal passages.
It is proven that the crests of Corythosaurus lacked holes and could not function for buoyancy, as water pressure at three meters would prevent lung inflation.
The genus Corythosaurus was described and named by Barnum Brown in 1914.
The holotype specimen, cataloged as AMNH 5240, was discovered in 1911 and secured in the fall of 1912 by Barnum Brown in Alberta within the Belly River Group.
Barnum Brown identified specific characteristics in 1914 to distinguish Corythosaurus from other Alberta hadrosaurids.
The holotype specimen was found as a carcass that had floated onto a beach, surrounded by water-worn bones and shells.

Corythosaurus fed on soft vegetation due to its shallow and delicate beak, and a preserved specimen contained conifer needles, seeds, twigs, and fruits in its chest cavity, indicating it was a browser.
Benson et al. (2012) estimated the average length of Corythosaurus to be 9 meters, while testing of a model concluded that the average weight was 3.82 tons.
Although once thought to be semi-aquatic due to webbed feet, the 'webs' were actually deflated padding similar to modern mammals.
Comparisons of scleral rings suggest Corythosaurus may have been cathemeral, active in short intervals throughout the day.
Corythosaurus likely possessed a sensitive middle ear, indicated by a thin stapes and large eardrum.
Researchers suggest the crest functioned for vocalization, acting like a trombone to amplify sound waves as the animal exhaled.

Corythosaurus is classified as a lambeosaurine, related to Lambeosaurus, Nipponosaurus, Velafrons, Hypacrosaurus, and Olorotitan, and is also classified as a hadrosaurid dinosaur within the subfamily Lambeosaurinae.
Corythosaurus casuarius is one of the few lambeosaurines with surviving fossilized juveniles assigned to the species.
Fossils of Corythosaurus have been found in the Oldman and Dinosaur Park Formations in Canada, where the animal lived approximately 77 to 75.7 million years ago.

It is debated regarding the exact structure of the crest, as Barnum Brown incorrectly identified the praemaxillae as nasals, and many presumed traits of the snout described by Brown are incorrect due to confusion between bone types.
Earlier paleontologists recognized four genera and thirteen species in the Dinosaur Park Formation based on size and crest shape differences, a classification now largely revised.
